scope: Corollary 6.4 (Stabilized contraction at a fixed scale) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-forces-rational-inessentiality-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 335 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dae319c1cc258208), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume ScalM ≥ κ > 0 and take the comparison data of Theorem 3.1 at scale R, so that L0 = J/R, log q ≤ JR. For all sufficiently large R, fix these data once and for all. Then for every finite k ≥ 1 there is a stabilized metric gk on Z × Tkq with scalar curvature at least κ/2, and a smooth map Fk : Z −→ Sq equal to a single value outside a compact set, with nonzero degree, such that |dFk|op ≤ C(q)4−k J/R. (6.16) The sphere has its standard unit metric. The constant C(q) is independent of k. If desired, the circle lengths may be increased so that the projection to the standard Tkq also has operator norm at most 4−kJ/R; this does not change scalar curvature or the bound on dFk.
